title: Transport an existing marked diagram under a specified base restriction
statement: Let f:X→S be any scheme morphism, U⊆S open containing a specified point η, g:V→U finite surjective universally injective, and U₀⊆U an open containing η. Fix σ:Z→V with gσ(Z)⊆U₀. Let finitely many diagrams Y_i→B_i→T_i→V commute with a finite surjection ν:∐Y_i→X_V. Suppose T_i→V is finite etale, Y_i→B_i open, B_i→T_i smooth proper, and W⊆X_V makes ν a thickening. Assume that for every s∈T_i mapping into U₀ the proper fibre is geometrically connected of dimension at most one and the marked open of Y_i maps onto s. Then restriction to U₀, regarded as an open U'⊆S, gives a finite radicial surjection V'→U', a lift σ':Z→V', an open immersion aV:V'→V compatible over S, and a restricted diagram of the same finite length. The restricted t_i remain finite etale, j_i open, p_i smooth proper with all fibres geometrically connected of dimension at most one, j_i p_i smooth surjective, ν finite surjective, and the restricted mark a thickening surjecting onto every T'_i. There are comparison arrows Y'_i→Y_i, B'_i→B_i, T'_i→T_i giving cartesian squares over aV and commuting with j_i,p_i. No field extensions or descent from a generic fibre are part of this statement. Empty schemes and empty index sets are permitted. [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]

proof.text: Let V₀=g⁻¹(U₀), U'=U.ι(U₀), and identify U₀ with U' using Scheme.Hom.isoImage. Put aV=V₀.ι and g'=(g restricted to U₀) followed by this isomorphism. Finiteness, surjectivity and universal injectivity follow from isPullback_morphismRestrict and iso invariance. Factor σ through aV using its assumed image condition. For each i take T'_i=T_i×_V V₀, B'_i=B_i×_V V₀ and Y'_i=Y_i×_V V₀. Define p'_i and j'_i by pullback.lift; pasting and cancellation of pullback squares give the component cartesian comparisons and the required arrow compatibilities.

Construct the cartesian square X×_S V₀→X×_S V over aV by pullback universality, and use it to define each Y'_i→X×_S V₀. Finite coproducts of these cartesian squares are cartesian (the proved source lemma AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_sigmaDesc). Their coproduct ν' is therefore finite and surjective by base change. The commuting triangles follow from pullback.lift_snd. Finite etaleness of t'_i, openness of j'_i and smooth properness of p'_i follow from their component pullback squares.

Every s∈T'_i maps to aT_i(s) whose image under t_i g lies in U₀, by the pullback equation and the membership proof carried by t'_i(s)∈V₀. Apply hgood there. The cartesian fibre square is Mathlib isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback; since aT_i is open, its residue-field map is an isomorphism, and so is the induced map on fibres. Geometric connectedness follows by base change; the topological dimension bound follows from the resulting homeomorphism.

Take W'=aX⁻¹(W). Given s∈T'_i, hgood supplies an old marked point y over aT_i(s). The cartesian square for j'_i p'_i supplies a point y' over both y and s. Its image is in W' by the cartesian comparison for ν', so the new marked open is surjective over T'_i. Forgetting membership gives surjectivity of j'_i p'_i; its smoothness follows by composition. Restrict the cartesian square for ν' to W using the proved source lemma AlgebraicGeometry.IsPullback.exists_isPullback_morphismRestrict. The restricted old ν is a closed immersion and surjective by hW, hence so is the new restricted ν. Conjugating by pullbackRestrictIsoRestrict gives the requested thickening in pullback form. Package these constructed objects, the comparisons, and all proved properties. This argument also covers n=0 and empty schemes.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_marked_curve_diagram_restriction
    {X S V Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (U : S.Opens) (η : S) (hη : η ∈ U)
    (g : V ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsFinite g] [Surjective g] [UniversallyInjective g]
    (U₀ : U.toScheme.Opens) (hη₀ : (⟨η, hη⟩ : U.toScheme) ∈ U₀)
    (σ : Z ⟶ V) (hσ : ∀ z : Z, g (σ z) ∈ U₀)
    (n : ℕ) (T Y B : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (t : ∀ i, T i ⟶ V)
    (j : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ B i) (p : ∀ i, B i ⟶ T i)
    (ν : (∐ Y) ⟶ pullback f (g ≫ U.ι)) [IsFinite ν] [Surjective ν]
    (hcomm : ∀ i, Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν ≫ pullback.snd f (g ≫ U.ι) = j i ≫ p i ≫ t i)
    (ht : ∀ i, IsFinite (t i) ∧ Etale (t i))
    (hj : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i)) (hp : ∀ i, Smooth (p i) ∧ IsProper (p i))
    (W : (pullback f (g ≫ U.ι)).Opens) (hW : IsThickening (pullback.snd ν W.ι))
    (hgood : ∀ i (s : T i), (t i ≫ g) s ∈ U₀ →
      GeometricallyConnected ((p i).fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
      topologicalKrullDim ((p i).fiber s) ≤ 1 ∧
      s ∈ Set.range (((Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν) ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ j i ≫ p i)) :
    ∃ (U' : S.Opens) (_ : η ∈ U') (V' : Scheme.{u}) (g' : V' ⟶ U'.toScheme),
      IsFinite g' ∧ Surjective g' ∧ UniversallyInjective g' ∧
      ∃ (aV : V' ⟶ V) (σ' : Z ⟶ V'),
        IsOpenImmersion aV ∧ σ' ≫ aV = σ ∧
        aV ≫ g ≫ U.ι = g' ≫ U'.ι ∧
        ∃ (T' Y' B' : Fin n → Scheme.{u})
          (t' : ∀ i, T' i ⟶ V') (j' : ∀ i, Y' i ⟶ B' i)
          (p' : ∀ i, B' i ⟶ T' i)
          (ν' : (∐ Y') ⟶ pullback f (g' ≫ U'.ι)),
          IsFinite ν' ∧ Surjective ν' ∧
          (∀ i, Sigma.ι Y' i ≫ ν' ≫ pullback.snd f (g' ≫ U'.ι) =
            j' i ≫ p' i ≫ t' i) ∧
          (∀ i, IsFinite (t' i) ∧ Etale (t' i)) ∧
          (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j' i)) ∧
          (∀ i, Smooth (j' i ≫ p' i) ∧ Surjective (j' i ≫ p' i)) ∧
          (∀ i, Smooth (p' i) ∧ IsProper (p' i) ∧
            ∀ s : T' i, GeometricallyConnected ((p' i).fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
              topologicalKrullDim ((p' i).fiber s) ≤ 1) ∧
          (∃ W' : (pullback f (g' ≫ U'.ι)).Opens,
            (∀ i, Surjective (((Sigma.ι Y' i ≫ ν') ⁻¹ᵁ W').ι ≫ j' i ≫ p' i)) ∧
            IsThickening (pullback.snd ν' W'.ι)) ∧
          ∃ (aY : ∀ i, Y' i ⟶ Y i) (aB : ∀ i, B' i ⟶ B i)
            (aT : ∀ i, T' i ⟶ T i),
            ∀ i,
              IsPullback (aY i) (j' i ≫ p' i ≫ t' i) (j i ≫ p i ≫ t i) aV ∧
              IsPullback (aB i) (p' i ≫ t' i) (p i ≫ t i) aV ∧
              IsPullback (aT i) (t' i) (t i) aV ∧
              j' i ≫ aB i = aY i ≫ j i ∧ p' i ≫ aT i = aB i ≫ p i
